CurrentLifecycle.bounds: One owner with two abstract content identities; one finite intent of fixed kind content/projection/restore; one non-idempotent product action with known/unknown accepted/unknown absent outcomes; at most one foreign writer; one current read; dispatch count 0..2.
CurrentLifecycle.assumptions: Metadata/body/dispatch/observation actions eventually return. Weak fairness covers operation dispatch, caller reinvocation with the original frozen input (including automatic matching resume), verification/finalization/retirement and an already-started read. Without these assumptions the model makes no eventual-success claim. Unknown absent ends in an explained blocked state with the intent retained.
CurrentLifecycle.scope: A ready owner has no content Operation while projection/restore may retain a separate finite intent. Completion qualification records the state at completion; a later writer does not retroactively invalidate a completed read. Same-page restore abstracts Trash as one bit and shares readiness guards. Bound create/update content steps use the content abstraction, but initial unbound creation/registration and terminal owner deletion are not represented: content Finish returns the owner to ready. Exact page identity, policy, budgets, physical retirement and Source parent/child cursors remain production regressions.

SourceSync.bounds: One Source, two affected Skill owners (one absent from the new target set), two commit/configuration identities, an existing owned or foreign finite intent, two verified child steps, at most one process restart and one upstream branch move.
SourceSync.assumptions: One cooperating content writer for the complete affected scope. Metadata/provider and finite-writer observations return; weak fairness applies to started coordination actions and the single reinvocation. Child steps abstract verified lower-writer results. Unknown results may reach blocked with their intent retained. No claim of cross-machine CAS, atomic multi-Skill writes, complete discovery or actual SDK/CLI/provider behavior.
SourceSync.scope: The coordinator distinguishes ready content from a pending finite input, refuses new upstream decisions before owned recovery, checks the union of old/new affected owners before Source mutation, freezes the observed commit for preparation, and requires both configuration and commit identity for a cheap no-op. Owned old projection recovery completes this invocation; a later invocation selects new upstream. Source success and later projection failure are independent results. Existing CurrentLifecycle and lower-writer regressions own non-idempotent dispatch and full child checkpoints. The source/test hashes below bind reviewed inputs, not an implementation refinement proof.

The hard-failure scenario stops before child allocation. Later recovery of a child whose old parent already has a hard result, or whose parent retired/changed generation, is outside this finite slice; production must verify the actual frozen Source/projection rather than treating those parents as successful local-cleanup proof.

A target cursor advances only after verification; completed target/source prefixes are not reentered, retryable items are not terminal, and hard failures remain in the final report. While this Source is the next unfinished member of the modeled active full batch, its verified successful child remains until the exact terminal result reaches the dispatch parent. AdmissionProgress.scope: Hints cannot reset total progress allowance and keep a request loading forever. NoDeadlock alone does not prove this temporal property. Real elapsed deadlines, cancellation and process-crash release require concrete tests.

InformationLimit.bounds: One cached version, at most one hidden remote edit and one consumption. The no-hidden-edits configuration excludes that edit; the limit configuration allows it.
InformationLimit.assumptions: The restricted control describes a remote object that does not change during the attempt. Allowing an unobserved edit deliberately falsifies exact remote equality at consumption time.
InformationLimit.scope: This positive/negative assumption control documents an information limit, not a production defect, product freshness guarantee, or implementation mutation.
